Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the summary. Appreciate the quick follow-up. A couple of clarifying questions before we schedule the tech deep-dive: 

1) For customer-managed keys (BYOK) — does Redwood support HSM-backed keys (e.g., AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM) or only KMS-wrapped keys? We need assurance that private key material never leaves an HSM boundary for our production tenant.

2) Is there a documented key-rotation process and separation of duties for key access? Who in Redwood (roles/team) can access plaintext keys or key material?

3) For data-at-rest: are full datasets encrypted per-tenant with unique CMKs, or is encryption applied at storage layer only? We also need any details you can provide about tokenization or additional controls you recommend for transaction metadata.

Attached is FinBank’s vendor security questionnaire (vendor security questionnaire.docx). Our procurement would like initial answers in ~72 hours if possible.

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the questions — I’ll outline our high-level positions below and attach a short KMS FAQ. Happy to expand on anything in the tech call.

Encryption-in-transit:
- All network traffic to our hosted API uses TLS 1.2+ (we recommend TLS 1.3), with strong cipher suites and mTLS options for Dedicated/Private deployments.

At-rest encryption:
- Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256. For our hosted offering, encryption is applied at the storage layer. For customer-isolated tenants (Dedicated/Private), we support per-tenant encryption keys (unique CMKs).

Key management and BYOK/HSM:
- We integrate with cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and support KMS-backed keys that are HSM-protected by the cloud provider.
- For customers requiring on-prem HSM or FIPS 140-2 Level 3, our Private deployment supports integration with customer-managed HSMs (BYOK) — key material never leaves the HSM boundary; Redwood references wrapped keys or uses KMS APIs for encryption/decryption calls in that model.
- We support both customer-provided CMKs (BYOK) and Redwood-managed keys. For BYOK, we provide guidance and scripts for key lifecycle, rotation, and importing public key material where applicable.

Access and separation of duties:
- Key management operations are limited to our platform security team and are audited. No engineer has direct access to plaintext key material in production. All KMS API calls are logged, and logs are retained per our retention policy (SOC 2 covered).

Rotation & lifecycle:
- We recommend a rotation cadence aligned with your policies (e.g., annual or semi-annual) and can automate re-wrapping procedures. We document rotation procedures in our security runbook and can provide the runbook snippets in the tech call.

SOC 2 coverage:
- Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II attestation (attached in Marissa’s email). Our SOC report covers encryption controls, access management, and change management for the inference platform. We can provide a SOC 2 bridge letter or specific control mappings on request.

Next steps:
- I’ll prepare succinct answers to the vendor questionnaire and export relevant controller/processor exhibits.
- Propose a 60-min technical session this week to demo key flows (wrap/unwrap, rotation) — please pick a time here: https://calendly.com/redwood/tech-deep-dive

Attached: kms-faq.txt

Regards,
